approachQuestion.prompt:
Build Order
A directed acyclic graph of V labeled tasks 0 through V−1 is supplied as outgoing adjacency lists. Edge u→v means u must precede v. Return the lexicographically smallest valid list of all task IDs. Example: V=4, edges=[(0,1)] → [0,1,2,3].

1 ≤ V ≤ 100000; 0 ≤ E ≤ 200000. No duplicate edges or self edges; acyclicity is guaranteed. Adjacency lists are read-only and need not be sorted. Lexicographic comparison uses the first differing ID. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 1 ≤ V ≤ 100000; 0 ≤ E ≤ 200000. No duplicate edges or self edges; acyclicity is guaranteed. Adjacency lists are read-only and need not be sorted. Lexicographic comparison uses the first differing ID.

options.text: Compute indegrees and put all zero-indegree tasks into a min-heap by ID. Remove its minimum, append it, decrement its outgoing neighbors’ indegrees, and insert each neighbor exactly when its indegree becomes zero.
options.feedback: Only zero-indegree tasks are eligible. Choosing the smallest eligible ID minimizes the next output position without violating any dependency, and repeating gives the lexicographically smallest full order.

options.text: Keep indegrees but find the next eligible task by scanning every unprocessed ID from smallest to largest after each output.
options.feedback: This gives the same smallest eligible choice, but rescans tasks whose eligibility has not changed.

options.text: Use a FIFO queue initially seeded by increasing zero-indegree IDs; append newly eligible IDs at its tail.
options.feedback: For the example, initial queue [0,2,3] leads to [0,2,3,1], while [0,1,2,3] is valid and lexicographically smaller.

options.text: Return task IDs in numerical order, ignoring edges.
options.feedback: For V=2 with edge 1→0, numerical order [0,1] violates the dependency.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A on the supplied outgoing adjacency lists with a binary min-heap and dense indegree array. Let V and E be vertex and edge counts. Build the initial zero-indegree heap bottom-up. No graph copy or hashing is used. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(E + V log(V+1)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(E + V log(V+1)) time, O(V+E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Process each edge once and each vertex through the available-ID heap once.
details: Indegree computation scans V vertices and E edges. Every vertex enters and leaves the heap once, and every edge is processed once. An edgeless graph has a large heap and requires sorting the candidate IDs through removals, giving the stated worst-case heap bound for this fixed method. The indegree array and heap use O(V); supplied edges are input, and the returned order is excluded.
“O(V+E) time, O(V) auxiliary space”: A FIFO queue can be linear but does not enforce the requested lexicographic order.
“O(V²+E) time, O(V) auxiliary space”: This describes rescanning every vertex per output; the heap avoids those scans.
“O(E + V log(V+1)) time, O(V+E) auxiliary space”: No adjacency copy is made, so E does not contribute auxiliary storage.
